correctness.rationale: For real z≥1 the leaf diagonal is invertible; the characteristic Schur factor z−a−Σ b_i c_i x_i y_i/(z−d_i) is increasing and diverges. Its sign at 1 decides whether there is a real eigenvalue >1, equivalent to supercriticality by nonnegativity even when some directions vanish. For fixed r=1−xy, the least spoke cost is min(p,q)r: (1−x)+(1−y)≥1−xy, with equality by attenuating only a cheaper direction. The linear budget binds, and an exchange orders reductions by cost per unit threshold mass, with at most one partial reduction in a greedy solution, not necessarily in every tied optimum. In the reciprocal problem the strictly concave separable penalized objective gives the claimed clipped t and a unique optimum; at least one term must be unclipped at H<W, on the strictly decreasing part of the multiplier curve. Every t>0. For paired equal prices, inserting the feasible t=√(1−r) gives the upper factor two, and the identical-spoke family gives exactly 2/(1+√u); unequal prices (1,M) at u=1/4 give 2(M+1)/3. Independent exact tests (python3 /workspace/reproduce_reviews.py 3) enumerate directed budget vertices and certify reciprocal points on two heterogeneous examples, including clipping (H=21/64, t=(1/4,1/8,1), costs 123/64 and 19/4). The frozen checker uses exact fractions for determinants and the directional cost, but floating bisection/tolerances for reciprocal examples, not exact rational certificates for that part; the proof and exact arithmetic examples settle those claims. This is an initial spectral threshold, not a final-size or extinction theorem.

value.rationale: The comparison answers a natural modeling question about changing the admissible controls under the same cost and threshold, not just evaluating a particular star. It determines when a greedy optimum can concentrate all intervention on a few directions, why reciprocity necessarily leaves every spoke with positive transmission factors, and how paired cost symmetry changes the sharp worst-case loss from unbounded to two. These are testable benchmarks for the specified matrix model, not claims about empirical intervention outcomes.
